title: Mock 1 · Foundations
blurb: Core definitions across all chapters plus a returns caselet: a gentle first lap.

questions.q: An investor's required rate of return is built from which three components, as per the workbook?
options: Dividend yield, capital gain and inflation
Coupon rate, current yield and YTM
Real risk-free rate, expected inflation and risk premium
questions.explanation: Section 1.4: investment earns (a) pure time value of money (real risk-free rate), (b) compensation for expected inflation and (c) a risk premium for uncertainty.
hints: These describe sources of realised equity return, not the required return.
These are bond yield measures.
These are performance/risk measures.
Correct: pure time value, inflation compensation and a premium for uncertainty.

questions.q: As per the dividend discount model, what is the intrinsic value of a share whose current dividend is ₹4, if dividends grow at 5% a year and the required return is 12%?
hints: Uses D0 instead of D1: 4/0.07.
Divides D0 by k only, ignoring growth.
Divides by g instead of (k - g).

questions.q: A 10-year bond with face value ₹100 and a 9% annual coupon trades at ₹112.50. What is its current yield?
questions.explanation: Current yield = annual coupon ÷ current market price = 9 ÷ 112.50 = 8.00%.
hints: That is the coupon rate (coupon/face value).
Current yield = 9/112.50 = 8%.
Inverts the premium relationship.
Wrong arithmetic.

questions.q: The counterparty risk in exchange-traded futures contracts is primarily mitigated through:
options: A bilateral collateral agreement between buyer and seller
Settlement on a gross basis between the two parties
The clearing corporation, which guarantees settlement
Position limits imposed on large traders
questions.explanation: Exchange trades are settled through a clearing corporation that provides novation and settlement guarantee (Chapter 2 and 5).
hints: Bilateral collateral is a feature of OTC deals.
Gross bilateral settlement increases, not reduces, counterparty risk.
Correct: the clearing corporation acts as buyer to every seller and seller to every buyer.
Position limits manage market concentration, not counterparty default.

questions.q: In the mutual fund structure in India, the custodian holding the scheme's assets is appointed by the:
questions.explanation: Section 6.3: custody of the assets is with a Custodian, who is appointed by the Trustees.
hints: Correct as per the workbook's description of the structure.
The AMC manages the money but does not appoint the custodian.
The sponsor creates the trust; the custodian is appointed by the trustees.
The RTA maintains investor records only.

questions.q: Under SEBI (Portfolio Managers) Regulations, 2020, what is the minimum net worth required to register as a portfolio manager?
questions.explanation: Section 7.4: before granting registration SEBI checks that the applicant fulfils the net worth requirement of ₹5 crore.
hints: Lower than the current requirement.
Correct: the applicant must fulfil the ₹5 crore net worth requirement.
₹50 lakh is the minimum client investment, not net worth.
Higher than required.

questions.q: A portfolio manager who manages funds strictly according to the directions of the client, with the client deciding what and when to buy or sell, is a:
questions.explanation: Section 7.2.2: in non-discretionary services the PM consults the client for every transaction and only executes.
hints: A discretionary PM exercises its own discretion.
In advisory, the client both decides and executes.
Correct: the manager executes, the client decides.
A co-investment PM is a special category, not defined by who decides trades.

questions.q: Which of the following charges is NOT permitted to be levied by a portfolio manager?
options: Performance fee above a hurdle rate
questions.explanation: SEBI circular of 13 February 2020: no upfront fees; brokerage charged at actuals; operating expenses capped at 0.50% p.a.
hints: Brokerage at actuals is charged as expense.
Fixed fees are allowed under the agreement.
Return-based fees are allowed as agreed.
Correct: no upfront fees shall be charged directly or indirectly (Reg. 22(11)).

questions.q: What is the first step in the portfolio management process?
questions.explanation: Section 9.3: steps are (1) policy statement, (2) study financial conditions and forecast, (3) construct the portfolio, (4) measure and evaluate.
hints: Construction is the third step.
Correct: the IPS is the road map.
Evaluation is the last step.
Studying conditions and forecasting is the second step.

questions.q: An individual is treated as resident in India in a previous year if he stays in India for:
options: 120 days or more during that year in all cases
365 days or more in the last 4 years only
182 days or more during that year
90 days or more during that year
questions.explanation: Section 10.1.1.1: resident if in India 182 days or more, or 60 days or more and 365 days or more in the preceding 4 years.
hints: 120 days applies only to citizens/PIOs with Indian income above ₹15 lakh in condition (b).
This is only half of the 60-day test.
Correct: the basic condition (a).
Not a condition in the Act.

questions.q: Under PMLA, intermediaries must record all cash transactions of a value more than:
questions.explanation: Section 11.1: records of all cash transactions of more than ₹10 lakh, or integrally connected series exceeding ₹10 lakh in a month.
hints: Lower than the threshold in the workbook.
Higher than the threshold.
Higher than the threshold.
Correct.

questions.q: Portfolio managers may invest client money in units of mutual funds only through:
options: Either plan, at the client's choice
questions.explanation: Section 11.4: the portfolio managers may invest in units of mutual funds only through direct plan.
hints: Correct: MF investments only via direct plans.
Regular plans carry distribution commission.
The regulation specifies direct plans.
No such restriction.

questions.q: The Dow Jones Industrial Average is an example of which type of index?
questions.explanation: Section 12.3.1: Dow Jones Industrial Average is a price weighted index computed by summing prices and dividing by a divisor.
hints: Sensex and NIFTY 50 are free-float weighted.
Equal weighting ignores price and size.
Correct: sum of prices ÷ divisor.
Fundamental indices weight on sales, book value etc.

questions.q: If a market is weak-form efficient, which analysis would be of little use in earning abnormal returns?
options: Fundamental analysis using new public information
Technical analysis based on past prices and volumes
questions.explanation: Section 13.5.1: weak-form EMH renders technical analysis irrelevant for superior returns.
hints: Semi-strong form deals with public information.
Strong form deals with insider information.
Diversification is unrelated to EMH tests.
Correct: weak form says past market data is fully reflected.

questions.q: An investor treats a tax refund as 'free money' and spends it on risky bets while being very careful with salary income. This is an example of:
questions.explanation: Section 14.3.2: mental accounting (Thaler) treats one sum differently from an equal sum depending on its mental account; windfalls get riskier treatment.
hints: Correct: money is treated as non-fungible based on its source.
Anchoring relies on a pre-existing reference number.
Status quo bias is doing nothing to avoid regret.
Endowment bias overvalues what one already owns.

questions.q: If the correlation between the two stocks in a portfolio decreases, everything else constant, the portfolio's risk will:
questions.explanation: Markowitz variance includes 2w1w2ρσ1σ2; a lower ρ lowers portfolio variance.
hints: Opposite direction.
Correct: lower correlation, more diversification benefit.
Correlation enters the variance formula directly.
The effect is predictable.

questions.q: The Security Market Line (SML) plots expected return against:
questions.explanation: Section 16.9: SML graphically depicts the relationship between systematic risk (beta) and expected return.
hints: The CML uses standard deviation.
Unsystematic risk is not priced in CAPM.
Tracking error is a performance measure.
Correct: the SML is the graphical form of CAPM.

questions.q: Non-market risk that is specific to a company or sector is also known as:
options: Unsystematic (idiosyncratic) risk, which can be reduced by diversification
Systematic risk, which can be reduced by diversification
Systematic risk, which can only be hedged
questions.explanation: Section 17.3.2: non-market risks are unique or idiosyncratic and can be reduced by diversification.
hints: Correct.
Systematic risk cannot be diversified away.
Non-market risk is not systematic.
Beta measures market (systematic) risk.

questions.q: Which of these is a PASSIVE equity portfolio strategy?
questions.explanation: Section 18.1: passive strategies include buy and hold and indexing (full replication and sampling).
hints: Sector rotation is an active, top-down strategy.
Correct: the portfolio mirrors the index.
Market timing is active.
Momentum is an active trading strategy.

questions.q: In a 'core and satellite' approach, the core portfolio typically forms about what share of the portfolio and how is it managed?
options: 70% to 80%, managed actively with high turnover
questions.explanation: Section 18.10: a portfolio generally has about 70% to 80% in the core (passive, low cost) and the balance in satellites (active).
hints: That describes the satellite portion.
The core is the majority and passive.
Correct.
The core has low turnover.

questions.q: A bond portfolio manager expects interest rates to rise significantly. What should she do with portfolio duration?
options: Keep duration unchanged and buy long-dated zero-coupon bonds
Extend maturity to lock higher yields
questions.explanation: Section 19.3.1: the manager would reduce the duration of the portfolio if she expects interest rates to rise.
hints: Correct: lower duration means less price loss as rates rise.
Higher duration magnifies the price fall.
Long zeros have the highest sensitivity.
Maturity extension increases price risk.

questions.q: Under which rebalancing strategy does the portfolio value become a function of the risky assets' performance, with no limit on upside?
questions.explanation: Section 21.4: under buy and hold the portfolio value becomes a function of the risky assets with no limit on upside.
hints: Constant mix sells winners, capping drift.
Correct: do-nothing strategy, unlimited upside.
CPPI dynamically shifts with the cushion.
Threshold rebalancing restores target weights.

questions.q: What is Ritu's holding period return for the year?
hints: Ignores the ₹1 lakh income.
Uses only the income plus half the gain.
Divides by the ending value incorrectly.
questions.case: Ritu invested ₹50 lakh in a discretionary PMS on 1 April. On 31 March the next year her portfolio was worth ₹57 lakh, and during the year she also received ₹1 lakh as dividends and interest. The portfolio's benchmark returned 10% over the same year, and the one-year risk-free rate was 6%. Ritu is in the 20% tax bracket for this income. There were no other cash flows.

questions.q: By how many percentage points did Ritu's portfolio beat its benchmark?
questions.explanation: Excess return over benchmark = 16% - 10% = 6%. (Some professionals call this simple excess 'alpha'.)
hints: Uses 14% (without income) minus 10%.
Uses 16% minus the 6% risk-free rate.
Arithmetic error.
questions.case: Ritu invested ₹50 lakh in a discretionary PMS on 1 April. On 31 March the next year her portfolio was worth ₹57 lakh, and during the year she also received ₹1 lakh as dividends and interest. The portfolio's benchmark returned 10% over the same year, and the one-year risk-free rate was 6%. Ritu is in the 20% tax bracket for this income. There were no other cash flows.

questions.q: What is Ritu's post-tax return, assuming the entire return is taxed at 20%?
questions.explanation: Post-tax return = pre-tax return x (1 - tax rate) = 16% x 0.8 = 12.8%.
hints: That is the pre-tax return.
Grosses up instead of taxing.
Divides 16 by 1.2.
